title: What are the fees?
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 2 Sep 2026). 5% platform fee on successful projects; Stripe card processing of roughly 3-5%; no fees if the goal is not reached; in the Pledge Manager, 5% of funds except taxes, with card processing on the full payment including taxes.

title: Why is funding all-or-nothing?
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 2 Sep 2026). Creators set goal and deadline, campaigns run 1 to 60 days, both locked at launch; no cap on overfunding; backers can cancel until the end and are charged only if the campaign succeeds; Kickstarter frames backing as funding a creative process, not a store purchase.

title: What is the maximum project duration?
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 6 Aug 2026). Projects run from 1 to 60 days; Kickstarter recommends 30 days or less, saying shorter campaigns often have higher success rates and more urgency; the deadline cannot change after launch.

title: How to set the right funding goal for your Kickstarter campaign
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 6 Aug 2026). The goal is the amount needed to complete the project, covering production, materials, shipping and fees; check delivery at exactly 100% and regret at 90%; shipping charged at pledge counts toward the total; larger goals generally have lower success rates; funds are generally taxable, ask an accountant; the Funding Calculator in the project editor adds the 5% fee and roughly 5% processing.

title: Setting up your project's pre-launch page
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 6 Aug 2026). Visitors click Notify me on launch; followers get an email at launch; pre-launch updates notify followers; follower count shows at 10 or more; launch is manual and cannot be scheduled; set up and share the page at least one week before launch.

title: What are the rules for hardware and product design projects?
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 6 Aug 2026). Hardware and product design projects must show a working prototype; photorealistic renderings are not permitted; creators must explain how the product will be made and whether they have made anything similar before.

title: Can I use AI-generated content or create AI technology in my project?
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 6 Aug 2026). Projects using AI tools must disclose which AI technology is used, how its output appears, and which parts are the creator's own work; projects building AI tools must list data sources and say whether consent and credit were handled.

title: Can I edit my rewards after I've launched my project?
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 6 Aug 2026). A tier or add-on that a backer has chosen generally cannot be changed: its estimated delivery date and existing shipping cannot be edited and items cannot be added; you can add shipping countries, raise quantity and add new tiers and add-ons while live; unbacked rewards can be edited or deleted.

title: How do I add Late Pledges to my project?
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 6 Aug 2026). Late Pledges let people back after the campaign at a separate late price per tier; Kickstarter suggests about 10% above the campaign price; must be enabled in draft or while live; same fees as campaign pledges; suggests ending them after 30 days with none.

title: Pledge Over Time FAQ
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page shows only 'updated over a week ago'). Backers pay in three equal payments, the first when the campaign succeeds and two monthly after; minimum pledges include USD 125, EUR 125, GBP 100, CAD 175 and AUD 200; creator enables it before launch; not available for Late Pledges; no extra fees; failed payments get 7 days (first charge) or 14 days (second and third) before the pledge is dropped.

title: What is a creator obligated to do once their project is funded?
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 6 Aug 2026). Creators must complete the project and deliver each reward as well as they can, be honest, post regular updates and tell backers promptly about delays; a creator who cannot finish must make every reasonable effort to reach a satisfying end for backers; refers to section 4 of the Terms of Use.

title: What should I post an update about and how often?
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 6 Aug 2026). Updates can cover anything about the project; the stated minimum is at least one update a month once funding is finished.

title: Does Kickstarter issue refunds?
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 6 Aug 2026). Kickstarter does not issue refunds; creators issue them at their discretion and should tell backers; refunds go to the original card and can take up to 30 days to appear.

title: What about marketing and promotion services that promise backers?
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 6 Aug 2026). Kickstarter endorses no marketing services; inflating backer numbers or paying for fake backers can lead to suspension; self-funding is prohibited; describes the large-pledge-then-sales-pitch scam; advises against binding manufacturing contracts until the project has funded and the payout has arrived.

title: Are creators based in the EU and UK responsible for VAT?
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 6 Aug 2026). In the Pledge Manager, Kickstarter collects VAT on items shipped to EU and UK backers where it is the deemed supplier or the creator authorises it; outside the Pledge Manager the creator is responsible; import duties are separate; Kickstarter says its tax services are not tax advice.

title: Recent Changes to EU Import Duties
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 6 Aug 2026). From 1 July 2026 the EU removed the duty exemption for goods under EUR 150 sent from outside the EU; a flat EUR 3 duty per item type applies until 1 July 2028; France and Italy add EUR 2 handling fees (from 1 March and 1 June 2026); DDP versus DDU; Kickstarter collects VAT for IOSS shipments but not duties.

title: Is a project video required to launch?
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 6 Aug 2026). A project video is not required but projects with compelling videos tend to do much better (no figure given); upload formats include MOV and MP4 up to 5120 MB; an optional Discovery Mode video is vertical 9:16, about 60 to 90 seconds, real people with the product, captions advised, key content kept off the edges.

title: Design for the Scroll: How to Make Your Kickstarter Page Easy to Understand
supports: Opened with WebFetch (published 19 Oct 2026). Many visitors skim images, headings and captions first; test by scrolling without reading; headings that name the question each section answers; one job per image; rewards easy to compare; check the page on a phone; useful alt text. No statistics.

title: What is the project collaborators tool and how do I use it?
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 17 Sep 2026). Collaborator permissions: edit project, manage community (post updates and comments, reply to messages), coordinate fulfilment, configure the Pledge Manager, analytics; collaborators cannot see detailed financial information, view payouts or issue refunds; they need their own Kickstarter account.

title: Fees
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 13 Oct 2026). 5% platform fee on crowdfunding; payment processing 3% plus a fixed 0.20 in the project currency per transaction; Pledge Manager and late pledges carry the same 5% plus processing with no setup fee; nothing is charged if the goal is not reached.

title: What changed with the Platform Upgrade?
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 13 Oct 2026). Migration on 16 Oct 2025 to a platform powered by Gamefound technology; Flexible Funding no longer offered for new campaigns; InDemand renamed Late Pledge; Perks renamed Rewards; pre-launch reservations discontinued; new campaigns onboard with Adyen; two-step review (compliance and KYC); reward prices entered net of tax; end dates cannot change once live; optional tips go to the creator.

title: General project settings
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 13 Oct 2026). Campaign end can be 24 hours to 60 days after launch; Endgame resets a 10-minute timer when someone pledges in the final 10 minutes, once per backer; after approval the launch date can only move later.

title: Launching crowdfunding campaign
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 13 Oct 2026). Publish a preview, set a launch date at least 7 days after submitting for review, review usually takes up to 3 business days, and the campaign starts automatically at the launch date once approved.

title: Order cancellation & Processing refunds
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 13 Oct 2026). Creators cancel orders or correct overcharges to refund; an Apply processing fee option deducts the transaction fee; refunds handled outside Indiegogo must be returned manually.

title: Crowdfunding Project Creator Settles FTC Charges of Deception
supports: Opened with WebFetch (press release 11 Jun 2015). Erik Chevalier raised more than 122,000 dollars from 1,246 backers for The Doom That Came to Atlantic City against a 35,000 dollar goal, cancelled after 14 months without rewards or refunds and spent most of the money on unrelated costs; the order bars him from misrepresenting campaigns and from failing to honour refund policies; a 111,793.71 dollar judgment was suspended.

title: Regulation Crowdfunding
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last reviewed or updated 24 Apr 2025). Up to 5 million dollars in 12 months; online only through an SEC-registered broker-dealer or funding portal; limits on how much non-accredited investors can invest; disclosure filings; securities generally cannot be resold for one year.

title: Funding Portals We Regulate
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 20 Oct 2026). A crowdfunding intermediary must register with the SEC as a broker or funding portal and join FINRA; the page lists funding portal members with SEC file numbers and marks suspended portals.

title: Crowdfunding
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 10 Jul 2026). Loan-based and investment-based crowdfunding are FCA-regulated and high-risk with no FSCS cover; donation-based and rewards-based or pre-payment crowdfunding are not FCA-regulated, though related payment services may be; contributors are unlikely to be protected if a project fails; use the FCA Firm Checker.

title: Regulation (EU) 2020/1503 on European crowdfunding service providers for business
publisher: EUR-Lex (Official Journal of the European Union)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Dated 7 Oct 2020; covers lending-based and investment-based crowdfunding services; excludes offers above EUR 5,000,000 over 12 months; the project owner draws up a key investment information sheet for each offer; applies from 10 Nov 2021 (Article 51).

title: Regulation (EU) 2023/988 on general product safety
publisher: EUR-Lex (Official Journal of the European Union)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Applies from 13 Dec 2024 (Article 52); Article 19 requires online and distance sellers to show the manufacturer's name and contact details, the EU responsible person where the manufacturer is outside the EU, product identification with a picture, and warnings in the local language; Article 16 requires an economic operator established in the EU.
